chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the fracture, where splints are upon it, or there is a wound with it, how should he deal with the wudu, and during the ghusl of janabah, and the ghusl of Jumu'ah. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should wash what the washing reaches from what is apparent, from what is not covered by the splints, and he should leave what is besides that from what he is not able to wash, and he should neither remove the splints nor tamper with the wound.'
ai.seo_question: How to perform wudu and ghusl with fractures and splints?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the principle of 'ease in difficulty' (taysir) within Shia fiqh, clarifying that ritual purity is maintained by washing only the accessible areas without necessitating the removal of splints or disturbing wounds. It reflects the juristic consensus that the obligation of washing is proportional to capability, preventing undue hardship during wudu and ghusl. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in balancing ritual purity with medical preservation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws about the fracture, the splints happen to be upon it, or there happens to be a wound with it, how should he deal with the Ablution (Wudhu), and during the major Ablution (Wudhu) (for sexual impurity), and the Friday washing. Heasws said: ‘He should wash what he can get to wash from what is apparent, from what there is no bandage over it, and he should leave what is besides that from that he is not able to wash it, and he should neither remove the bandage nor tamper with the wound’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, al-Rida, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about how to go about for Wudu’ on a broken part (to be washed or wiped for Wudu’) with bandage or a wound on them, or when taking a Ghusl (bath) due to sexual relation or Friday Ghusl (bath). He (the Imam) said, ‘One must wash the parts that are not covered by the bandage and leave the parts that are not accessible because of it, one must not remove the bandage and must not play around with the wound.”’
